CveFindings.Name: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions in Newtonsoft.Json
CveFindings.Description:
[CVE-2024-21907](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5crp-9r3c-p9vr): Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions in Newtonsoft.Json

Severity: HIGH

Affected dependencies:
  - Newtonsoft.Json:6.0.4 (declared at eShopLegacyNTier/src/eShopWinForms/packages.config:5)

Recommended fix:
  - Upgrade Newtonsoft.Json to 13.0.1 or later

CweFindings.Name: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime
CweFindings.Description: The product does not release a resource after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the resource is no longer needed.
CweFindings.Explanation: Program.Main creates eShopServiceReference.CatalogServiceClient (a WCF ClientBase, which must be closed) at line 584 and never closes or disposes it.

CweFindings.Name: Missing Synchronization
CweFindings.Description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.
CweFindings.Explanation: CatalogService.CreateCatalogItem (lines 141-144) and CreateAvailableStock (lines 187-190) compute the next primary key as Max(Id)+1 and save without any locking or transaction, so concurrent WCF calls can generate duplicate keys or lose updates.

CweFindings.Name: Insufficient Logging
CweFindings.Description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.
CweFindings.Explanation: The WCF service performs create, update and remove operations on catalog data (lines 139-157) without any audit or security event logging; no logging framework is used anywhere in the solution.
